questions.q: Where do you run a SOQL query in Workbench?
options: Migration menu, then Deploy
Data menu, then Purge
Queries menu, then SOQL Query
Utilities menu, then Apex Execute only
questions.explain: The SOQL Query page is under the Queries menu.

questions.q: What are two ways to define a query on the SOQL Query page?
options: Pick object, fields, filter and sort, or write raw SOQL
Upload a Flow, or paste an Apex class
Use only a drag-and-drop report builder
Type a natural-language question
questions.explain: The page supports both a guided builder and raw SOQL text.

questions.q: How does SOQL written in Workbench differ from SOQL in other tools?
options: Workbench requires a different query language
Workbench doesn't allow WHERE clauses
Workbench only allows SELECT *
It doesn't; it's the same language with the same clauses and functions
questions.explain: SOQL is SOQL: the same syntax and limits apply wherever you run it.

questions.q: How can you look up a field's exact API name before writing a query?
options: Guess based on the field label
Info menu, Standard & Custom Objects, then choose the object
Run SELECT * on the object
Check the Data menu
questions.explain: The object describe view lists every field, its API name and its type.

questions.q: Why is SELECT * a bad idea to try in Workbench?
options: Workbench blocks all queries that include Id
It would delete records
SOQL has no SELECT *; you must name each field
It only works on custom objects
questions.explain: SOQL requires explicit field names in every tool, as covered in Lesson 1.
